title: Janapada of Vatsa
capsule: Vatsa was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of Iron Age northern India, centered on Kauśāmbī (modern Kosam, Uttar Pradesh) on the Yamunā river, and traced its ruling lineage to the Kuru dynasty whose king Nicakṣu relocated there after Hastinapura was destroyed by flooding. Its most historically attested king, Udayana (c. 6th–5th century BCE), was a contemporary of the Buddha and a figure prominent in Buddhist and Jain narratives; his mother Mṛgāvatī served as regent and is among the earliest named female rulers in Indian history. Vatsa was first subdued by Avanti under Pradyota and subsequently annexed into Magadha by the Shishunaga dynasty. The kingdom controlled the lower Doab and was a significant node in the Buddhist missionary networks of the period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kauśāmbī's location is confirmed archaeologically; broader territorial limits of the Vatsa Janapada for the 600–450 BCE window are inferred from textual sources and cannot be mapped with precision.
